entry.subject: Axle magnetic-field metrology and copper-versus-brass electromagnetic screen
entry.trigger: Need to measure the magnetic field generated around the operating Axle and understand the effect of a copper or brass Axle body.
research_result: Copper and brass are approximately non-ferromagnetic structural candidates; their important difference in this branch is electrical conductivity rather than magnetic permeability.
NIST conductivity anchor: copper about 57 MS/m, brass C260 about 15.5 MS/m, making copper much more capable of supporting induced currents for comparable geometry.

The Axle's own rigidly co-rotating permanent-magnet field is approximately stationary in the rotor material frame; the important eddy-current drivers are stator field, harmonics, asymmetry, EPM switching and stationary conductive structures seeing the rotating field.
Coreless/slotless AFPM remains the baseline starter-generator; conductive structures near its time-varying air-gap field must be explicitly loss-tested.

Preliminary electromagnetic material preference moves toward a lower-conductivity brass-class non-ferromagnetic Axle body rather than solid copper, but the exact brass alloy must pass wet corrosion/dezincification and mechanical tests.

calculation_checkpoint.interpretation: At JANUS screening speeds the relevant skin depths remain in millimetres/centimetres; a few-mm conductive Axle is not a perfect shield, but eddy drag, heating and phase distortion can still be significant.

entry.measurement_plan: Map Bx/By/Bz synchronized with encoder angle, RPM, current, torque and temperature at PM-static, passive-spin, motor, generator and optional EPM states; repeat with geometrically matched Cu and brass bodies/sleeves.
entry.next_decision: Do not freeze copper or brass by intuition. Freeze the material only after equal-geometry A/B measurements of drag watts, B-field distortion, heat, corrosion/water compatibility and mechanical behavior.
